finding.class: tooling-integrity (the S27/S28/S30 family — this time: the environment precondition no probe verified)
finding.surface: dev-server boot stability — the stale Turbopack .next/dev cache reload loop

capturedFailureState.trigger: mid-suite daemon restart after an unclean pkill (Turbopack mid-cache-write)
capturedFailureState.symptom: the connectivity audit failed OPAQUELY — page.click timeout 30000ms on the disabled login submit button; the Playwright log showed 'element was detached from the DOM, retrying' + repeated 'navigated to http://localhost:3000/login'

diagnosticProbe.method: framenavigated recording (main frame) + hydration observation over a 15s window on /login
diagnosticProbe.note: React never hydrated; form fills were discarded on every reload; the button stayed disabled={busy || !email || !password} because the input events never landed in hydrated state

capturedFailureState.httpHealthDuringLoop: {"status":"ok","db":"up","app":"studyflow"} — /api/health 200 and /login 200 (29ms warm) WHILE the route reload-looped: liveness ≠ stability ≠ hydration (the AP-76 lesson)

differentialProof.step1_restartWithoutCacheClear: daemon restarted cleanly (fresh boot, health ok, /login 200) — the reload loop PERSISTED (connectivity audit failed twice more; the diagnostic probe captured 17+ navs/15s)
differentialProof.step2_cacheClear: pkill + rm -rf .next/dev (282MB Turbopack incremental cache) + restart — the loop is GONE: login completes end-to-end (button enables after fill; click lands on /Dashboard)
differentialProof.conclusion: the stale state lives IN .next/dev, not in the daemon process — the S9 lesson's 'restart the daemon cleanly' remedy is INSUFFICIENT for this variant

nonDeterminism.control: a deliberate unclean kill (pkill after warming /login) + restart WITHOUT the cache clear did NOT reproduce the loop a second time
nonDeterminism.interpretation: the corruption requires a kill mid-cache-write (the audits hammering /login while Turbopack wrote route cache entries); intermittent + opaque = exactly the class a future session would misdiagnose as an app defect ('the login button never enables') and fix in the wrong layer
